hero.lead: A nation of 6.4 million with farmland across almost half its land, public debt of 29.9% of GDP and a €6.17 billion recovery and resilience plan.

capital.heading: Low debt, and sanitation and incomes to build.

record.text: Recovery and resilience plan, all in grants (the Council approved €6.3 billion on 3 May 2022)
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Reopening of three euro bonds due 2032, 2038 and 2045
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · 7 July 2026 · €1bn added to the 2032 issue, €1bn to the 2038 issue and €500M to the 2045 issue · re-offer yields 3.49%, 4.27% and 4.67%
register.note: Order book for the additional issuance above €9.5 billion
register.text: A €2.5 billion reopening of three existing euro bonds of the Republic of Bulgaria, sold to international investors at spreads of 60, 115 and 140 basis points over mid-swaps. Sovereign bonds fund the state budget, from which the public services behind the seven standards are paid.

register.name: Dual-tranche euro bonds due 2034 and 2038
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · priced 28 April 2025 · settled 7 May 2025 · €2.25bn 9-year at 3.500%, due 7 May 2034 · €1.75bn 13-year at 4.125%, due 7 May 2038
register.note: Final order books of €4.9 billion for the 9-year and €3.6 billion for the 13-year tranche; re-offer yields 3.681% and 4.332%
register.text: Two new benchmark bonds of the Republic of Bulgaria, €2.25 billion and €1.75 billion, sold to international investors. The Ministry of Finance states that the proceeds go to general budget purposes, the refinancing of existing debt and the fiscal reserves; the budget pays for the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · €6,174 million in grants · fourth instalment: disbursement authorised 24 July 2026, partly suspended
register.note: Approved by the Council of the EU on 3 May 2022 at €6.3 billion; the Commission now states €6.17 billion in grants
register.text: EU grants under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Bulgaria, paid in instalments as it meets its milestones and targets. The Commission authorised the third instalment on 22 December 2025 and the fourth on 24 July 2026, in each case with part of the payment suspended.

register.name: CARMEN smart grid project: EU grant to the Electricity System Operator
register.detail: Connecting Europe Facility · grant agreement signed 22 May 2026, Copenhagen · investments of more than €59M in Bulgaria, 50% EU grant · joint project with Romania
register.note: CARMEN budget of nearly €208 million in all, 50% grant funds; Bulgarian works to the end of 2032
register.text: An EU grant to the Electricity System Operator (ESO) for its part of CARMEN, a smart grid project with Romania: the reconstruction and automation of the Dobrudzha, Varna, Gorna Oryahovitsa, Mizia and Balkan substations, and optical telecommunication rings on over 1,100 km of overhead lines, including two interconnectors with Romania. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Programme Environment 2021–2027: new Water Sustainability priority
register.detail: Programme amendment approved by the European Commission · announced 18 March 2026 · agglomerations of 5,000 to 10,000 population equivalents
register.note: European funding for water supply and sanitation infrastructure in smaller agglomerations
register.text: EU funding under a new priority of Programme Environment 2021–2027 for water supply and sanitation infrastructure in agglomerations of 5,000 to 10,000 population equivalents, which the Ministry of Environment and Water also links to depopulation in small settlements. It serves the shelter standard, where safely managed sanitation is furthest from reach, and the water standard.

register.name: EU funds co-financing loan 2021–2027 (structural programme loan)
register.detail: EIB · approved 18 September 2024 · €250M signed 12 December 2024 · €250M signed 17 September 2025, in force 11 December 2025 · credit line of up to €1bn
register.note: Signed by sector, among others: water and sewerage €20M, education €20M, health €15M, solid waste €45M
register.text: EIB loans to the Republic of Bulgaria for the national share of projects co-financed by EU funds in 2021–2027, including the improvement of water and waste management systems. Two finance contracts of €250 million each are signed, of a credit line of up to €1 billion; they serve the water, shelter, education and health standards among others.

register.name: Framework loan for EU co-financing 2021–2027: education and skills
register.detail: CEB · approved 27 September 2024 · signed 25 June 2025 · ratified 6 November 2025 · in force 25 November 2025
register.note: Partly finances two operational programmes dedicated to education
register.text: A Council of Europe Development Bank loan to the Government of Bulgaria for the national share of programmes co-financed by the European Social Fund Plus: education, vocational training and the employability of the workforce. It serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Programme Environment 2021–2027: water and sewerage contracts with seven water companies
register.detail: Ministry of Environment and Water · signed 10 February 2025 · 21 agglomerations · total budget BGN 1,061.9M
register.note: Grant of BGN 761.7 million within a total budget of BGN 1,061.9 million
register.text: Grants under Programme Environment 2021–2027 to seven water and sewerage companies for 10 wastewater treatment plants, 223.89 km of sewage network, 6 drinking water treatment plants and 218.50 km of water supply network reconstruction. It serves the shelter standard, where safely managed sanitation is furthest from reach, and the water standard.

register.name: Tenevo battery energy storage system
register.detail: EBRD · senior loan to Tenevo Solar Technologies · announced November 2026 · 246 MW / 512.5 MWh · with Raiffeisen Bank International
register.note: Financing of €60 million in all with Raiffeisen Bank International
register.text: An EBRD loan for a battery storage system of 246 MW and 512.5 MWh at Tenevo, in south-eastern Bulgaria, alongside Raiffeisen Bank International. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: EIB Group securitisation for new lending by Allianz Bank Bulgaria
register.detail: EIF and EIB · announced 5 June 2026 · synthetic securitisation of about €252M of SME and consumer loans · protection on a €30.3M mezzanine and an about €219M senior tranche
register.note: New lending to SMEs and mid-caps over three years, more than €80 million of it for climate action
register.text: The EIB Group takes on the credit risk of part of Allianz Bank Bulgaria’s loan book, so that the bank can lend around €340 million more to small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps over three years. It serves the livelihood standard, with more than €80 million of the new lending directed to climate action and environmental sustainability.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.4% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Habitat for Humanity Bulgaria
items.text: An organisation that runs revolving home improvement funds with local partners, lending vulnerable families, predominantly Roma, interest-free sums of up to €600 for urgent repairs such as leaking roofs and sanitary facilities, repaid within a year. From 2014 to 2020 it supported 3,345 households through 2,137 microloans, with repayment above 95%.

items.name: Bulgarian Food Bank
items.text: The largest national charity working to reduce food insecurity in Bulgaria: it rescues surplus food and distributes essential products through nearly 330 frontline charities, services and community groups. In 2026 it supports more than 88,000 elderly people, children and families facing hardship.

items.name: Jamba
items.text: A career hub for people with disabilities, launched in Sofia in 2017, with a café and catering service and a training kitchen for people seeking catering jobs. Hundreds of people with disabilities have found stable employment through it.

items.name: The Social Teahouse
items.text: A Bulgarian social enterprise that supports people with intellectual disabilities or from vulnerable backgrounds through job training and mentorship, one of the employment-focused social enterprises in the Social Enterprise World Forum’s Bulgarian case studies of 2025.

items.name: Joy for our Children
items.text: An organisation that runs a bakery where children and young people build working skills in a protected environment, with the goal of paid jobs. Its founders are alumni of the Reach for Change programme in Bulgaria.
